subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should Claw-owned cron teardown remain a provenance-aware Claw lifecycle operation that composes shared deletion primitives, or should canonical `agents delete` become responsible for all agent-owned scheduler cleanup before this feature lands?
rationale: The earlier review requested canonical deletion ownership, while the branch discussion says ordinary agent deletion intentionally remains unchanged and later repairs implement a convergent Claw-specific path; this is a durable cross-feature ownership contract, not a mechanical follow-up.

options.title: Ratify Claw-specific teardown
options.body: Keep ordinary `agents delete` unchanged and document/test the provenance-aware Claw removal path as the sole owner of Claw-installed cron cleanup.

options.title: Centralize agent cron cleanup
options.body: Move agent-owned cron teardown into canonical agent deletion and make Claw removal layer only its provenance and managed-workspace cleanup around that operation.

recommendation.title: Ratify Claw-specific teardown
recommendation.body: Keep ordinary `agents delete` unchanged and document/test the provenance-aware Claw removal path as the sole owner of Claw-installed cron cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review history and latest repair commits connect Patrick-Erichsen most directly to the deletion-lifecycle contract.
